The best positive signals were limited procedural reforms and partial clemency, not a sustained pattern of promise-keeping or honest disclosure.","evidence":[{"title":"President El-Sisi’s Speech at the “Egyptian Family Iftar”","publisher":"Presidency of the Republic of Egypt","date":"2024-04-06","url":"https://www.presidency.eg/EN/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news642024-2/","summary":"Sisi publicly renewed his promise at the start of the new term and described the election as “fair and honorable.” This is useful as a self-claim, but it reads as self-justification rather than independently verified candor, and it is contradicted by rights reporting on the pre-election environment.","question_ids":["7B.8","7B.7"]},{"title":"Egypt: Lift travel bans imposed on two human rights lawyers","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-07-09","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-lift-travel-bans-imposed-on-two-human-rights-lawyers/","summary":"The authorities announced the closure of Case 173 in March 2024 and lifted most travel bans tied to it, which is a real but limited sign of easing pressure on civil society. Amnesty also notes that some bans and asset-freeze effects persisted, so this was partial, not a broad accountability turn.","question_ids":["7B.8","7B.6","7B.7"]},{"title":"President El-Sisi Directs the Referral of the National Dialogue’s Recommendations to the Government","publisher":"Presidency of the Republic of Egypt","date":"2024-08-21","url":"https://www.presidency.eg/EN/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news2182024/","summary":"Sisi publicly ordered the government to implement National Dialogue recommendations on pretrial detention, alternatives to detention, and compensation for wrongful detention. This is the clearest official pro-reform signal I found in 2024, but it is narrow and remains official self-reporting.","question_ids":["7B.8","7B.7"]},{"title":"Presidential decree pardoning defendants on occasion of Police Day, January 25 Revolution","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"2024-01-13","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/presidential-decree-pardoning-defendants-on-occasion-of-Police-Day-January-25-Revolution/","summary":"Sisi issued a pardon for some defendants, including people convicted for political expression or political activity. This is a genuine positive signal, but it is episodic clemency rather than a durable pattern of honoring dissent or accepting scrutiny.","question_ids":["7B.8","7B.6"]},{"title":"Egypt: Court Punishes Activists for Challenging al-Sisi","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-02-08","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/08/egypt-court-punishes-activists-challenging-al-sisi","summary":"A Cairo court sentenced Ahmed Tantawy and supporters for peaceful political activism tied to his presidential challenge, and barred Tantawy from future elections for five years. That is strong evidence against keeping promises about fair competition and against respecting the formal spirit of electoral rules.","question_ids":["7B.8","7B.6","7B.7"]},{"title":"Egypt: Spate of Free Speech Prosecutions","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-08-29","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions","summary":"Egyptian authorities arbitrarily detained and prosecuted critics, including cases tied to reporting on corruption investigations involving senior pro-Sisi party members. This is direct evidence of punishing scrutiny and shielding associates rather than handling criticism transparently.","question_ids":["7B.8","7B.6","7B.7"]},{"title":"Egypt: Freedom in the World 2024 / Freedom on the Net 2024","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says Egypt continued blocking independent and journalistic sites, had 562 blocked websites/links by June 2024, allowed censorship without judicial approval, and upheld the rejection of Mada Masr’s licensing request. This is strong evidence that the state manipulated public information and constrained independent verification of official conduct.","question_ids":["7B.8","7B.7","7B.6"]},{"title":"Egypt: Freedom in the World 2024 / Freedom on the Net 2024","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-net/2024","summary":"Freedom House says Egypt continued blocking independent and journalistic sites, had 562 blocked websites/links by June 2024, allowed censorship without judicial approval, and upheld the rejection of Mada Masr’s licensing request. This is strong evidence that the state manipulated public information and constrained independent verification of official conduct.","question_ids":["7B.8","7B.7","7B.6"]}]}
